title: A toy car gets pushed along in simple eighteen-month play
summary: By about 18 months, most children play with toys in a simple way, such as pushing a toy car, the U.S. CDC says.
body: Playing with toys in a simple way, like pushing a toy car, is the cognitive example on the CDC 18-month page. The page's standard is a skill seen in 75 percent or more of children, not in every child. Learn the Signs. Act Early. materials, it says, are not a substitute for standardized, validated developmental screening tools. Copying a grown-up who sweeps with a broom is the neighboring cognitive line and is not restated. Pushing the car is object play. It does not judge one child, and another nation may list different play.
